name: Breadth-First Search
instructions: Implement breadth-first search using a non-recursive queue-based approach.
help: Keep the paths that are still to be explored in a queue (a list): take them from the front with pop(0), and add new ones at the back with append.
Start with a queue that holds the path (start,). Take the first path: if it ends at the goal, return it. Otherwise, add one longer path for each neighbor of its last node.
Skip neighbors that are already on the path, so you don't walk in circles. If the queue runs empty, there is no path: return None.

    "def depth_first_search(\n",
    "    graph: list[tuple[str, str, int]], start: str, goal: str\n",
    ") -> tuple[str, ...] | None:\n",
    "    \"\"\"Return a path from start to goal using depth-first search.\"\"\"\n",
    "    stack = []\n",
    "    stack.append((start,))\n",
    "    while stack:\n",
    "        path = stack.pop()\n",
    "        node = path[-1]\n",
    "        if node == goal:\n",
    "            return path\n",
    "        for neighbor in reversed(neighbors(graph, node)):\n",
    "            if neighbor in path:\n",
    "                continue\n",
    "            stack.append(path + (neighbor,))\n",
    "    return None"
   ]
